map.Lessons 4-3, 4-4 & 4-5 — estimate percen: Lessons 4-3, 4-4 & 4-5. Estimate percents. Find them for real. Then work them back. Four reader gates block the night market goal.
map.Previously: the hundred-bulb lantern boa: Last time: a board of a hundred lights. It showed the whole market: percent means per hundred. The glitch still flickers near Bram's stall.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: Hana's lantern: Last time, in Episode 1: Hana's board made the pier goal one hundred lights. Bram had to say what "per hundred" means. Tonight the fair is in full swing.
map.Halfway night! I'm running the fund trac: It is halfway night! I keep the fund chart. I write down each pledge. I check it. I add it to the chart.
map.No time to double-check anything, kids!: No time to check, kids! Hot sales check themselves!
map.For the record: nothing at that stall ha: Note: no one at that stall checks twice. Tonight we keep OUR numbers true. Fast ones first.
map.The games alley. Tokens everywhere, and: The games alley. Tokens are all over. The line will not wait for long division.
map.Booth rules: 24% of these 81 ring-toss t: Booth rules: 24% of these 81 tokens win prize stamps. The line wants a number NOW. Not a worksheet.
map.So estimate it. 24% is one step from a b: So estimate it. 24% is close to a benchmark. Benchmarks are fast.
map.Estimation protocol: trade ugly numbers: Here is how to estimate. Swap hard numbers for easy ones. Change the percent to a benchmark: 10%, 25%, 50%. Then change the number to one that fits it.
map.To estimate a percent of a number, round: To estimate a percent of a number, round both. Make the percent a benchmark. Make the number one that splits evenly. Close and fast beats exact and late.
map.Speed round, reader — two estimates, zer: Speed round, reader! Two estimates. Do them in your head. The line is watching.
map.No calculators in the games alley. Snap: Do it in your head. Change each percent to a benchmark. Change each number to an easy one. Then pick the best estimate.
map.Prize stamps — about how much is 24% of: Prize stamps. About how much is 24% of 81 tokens?
map.Fund-table stoppers — about how much is: At the fund table. About how much is 52% of 198 people?
map.Conceptual: estimating means trading for: Conceptual: to estimate, use easy numbers. 24% is right next to 25%. That is one quarter. 52% is right next to 50%. That is one half.
map.Procedural: a quarter of a number is the: Procedural: a quarter of a number is the number ÷ 4. 81 is close to 80. Half of a number is the number ÷ 2. 198 is close to 200.
map.Estimates got us through the rush. The l: Estimates got us through the rush. Now the book wants the REAL numbers. The fund can't use an "about."
map.Percent OF a number means multiply — aft: Percent OF a number means multiply. But first, make the percent a decimal.
map.And once a percent becomes an amount, yo: Then the percent becomes an amount. Now you can compare it to real dollars.
map.To find a percent of a number, rewrite t: Want a percent of a number? Write the percent as a decimal (30% = 0.30). Then multiply. The ÷100 hides in the % sign.
map.Reader — chalk the real amounts. The led: Reader, write the real amounts. The book does not take "about."
map.The ledger wants exact. The Garcia pledg: The book wants exact numbers. The Garcia pledge: 30% of $140 is paid tonight. The gift bundles: 15% of 60 lanterns are kept. Find both for real.
map.Conceptual: 'percent OF a number' means: Conceptual: 'percent OF a number' means multiply. But first, make the percent a decimal. The ÷100 hides in the % sign.
map.Procedural: 30% = 0.30, so multiply 0.30: Procedural: 30% = 0.30, so multiply 0.30 × 140. Or find 10% of 140 and times it by 3. 15% = 0.15, so multiply 0.15 × 60. Or take 10% of 60. Then add half of that.
map.Closing-rush inventory. Two stalls, two: The end of the rush. Two stalls, two counts. No one wrote down the start totals.
map.This time we KNOW the part. The mystery: This time we KNOW the part. We need the whole. How big is the roll? How big is the batch?
map.Reverse protocol: whole = part ÷ percent: Work back: whole = part ÷ percent-as-a-decimal. You split by a number less than one. That makes the part GROW back to its hundred. The whole is bigger than its part.
map.The whole is the original 100%. Know a p: The whole is the first 100%. Do you know a part and its percent? Divide: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). Then multiply to check.
map.Run it backwards, reader — rebuild both: Work back, reader. Find both wholes before the cart leaves.
map.Closing-rush inventory. The booth sold 2: End of the rush. The booth sold 24 tickets. That is 40% of the roll. The stand sold 18 skewers. That is 25% of tonight's batch. Find each WHOLE.
Conceptual: this time you KNOW the part. The whole is the first 100%. So the whole must be BIGGER than the part.
map.Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a: Procedural: whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). Tickets: 24 ÷ 0.40. Skewers: 18 ÷ 0.25. Then multiply to check.
map.Late evening. The thermometer ticks past: Late at night. The chart passes its sixtieth light. Then Bram finds a megaphone.
map.Attention, market! Sixty percent done me: Listen up, market! Sixty percent done means just SIXTY DOLLARS to go! We are done! Go home happy!
map.That's not how percents work — and if th: That is not how percents work. If the crowd believes him, the gifts stop COLD.
map.Distortion spike. A percent is not an am: Glitch spike. A percent is not an amount. 60% turns into dollars only with its whole. The crowd is about to leave. Work fast.
map.Three locks before the crowd drifts: the: Three locks before the crowd leaves. The FULL goal. What is still missing. What went wrong in Bram's words.
The sign is true. The megaphone is not. Reader, take the boss.
map.Boss Gate: the thermometer gives you a p: Boss Gate: the chart gives you a part ($540) and its percent (60%). Work back to the whole. Then work on to what is left.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The thermometer: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The chart knows its part. You must find the whole.
map.The pier-fund thermometer reads $540 rai: The fund chart reads $540 raised — 60% of the goal. Bram's megaphone says: "60% done means only 60 dollars to go!" The crowd leaves. Three locks:
map.Bram claims \"60% done means only 60 dol: Bram says this: "60% done means only 60 dollars to go!" What is wrong?
map.Conceptual: $540 is the PART and 60% is: Conceptual: $540 is the PART. 60% is its percent. The goal is the WHOLE. Work back to find it. Then see what is left to raise.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: goal = 540 ÷ 0.60. L: Procedural: Lock 1: goal = 540 ÷ 0.60. Lock 2: still needed = goal − 540. That is the last 40% of the goal.
map.Nine hundred. Chalked, checked, and TRUE: Nine hundred. Checked and TRUE. The crowd is back. Bram holds his megaphone upside down. He is ashamed.
map.Fine. FINE. Three hundred sixty to go. I: Fine. FINE. Three hundred sixty to go. Next time I will check the megaphone.
map.One night was never the whole story. To: One night was not the whole story. More to come…
map.Estimate it.Snap the percent to a benchm: Estimate it.Change the percent to a benchmark (10%, 25%, 50%). Change the number to an easy one. Close and fast beats exact and late.
map.Compute it.Percent OF a number = decimal: Compute it.Percent OF a number = decimal × number. The ÷100 hides in the % sign. 30% is 0.30. It is never just 30.
map.Reverse it.Know a part and its percent?: Reverse it.Do you know a part and its percent? whole = part ÷ (percent as a decimal). The whole is bigger than its part.
map.The megaphone trap.A percent is not an a: The megaphone trap.A percent is not an amount. "60%" turns into dollars only with its whole. The whole was $900. It was not $600.
map.\"A percent without its whole is a rumor: "A percent with no whole is just talk. Find the whole. Then the talk becomes math." — A.V.
map.completed Unit 4 · Episode 2: Find the W: did Unit 4 · Episode 2: Find the Whole. You can estimate percents. You can find the percent of a number. You know a part and its percent. You can find the whole.
map.The full story — Vol. 4: The Hundred Mar: The full story, Vol. 4: The Hundred Market, waits at the market gate.
map.Different booth: about how much is 26% o: New booth: about how much is 26% of 121 tokens?
map.One quarter of 120 = 30. So 26% of 121 i: One quarter of 120 = 30. So 26% of 121 is about 30. Fast and close enough.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Different tag: 20% of a $35 crate goes t: New tag: 20% of a $35 crate goes to the fund.
map.0.20 × 35 = 7 — so $7 to the fund. Decim: 0.20 × 35 = 7. So $7 goes to the fund. Decimal first. Then multiply. Every time.
map.Different stand: 21 cocoa cups is 30% of: New stand: 21 cups is 30% of the night's supply.
21 ÷ 0.30 = 70 cups in the full supply. Multiply to check: 0.30 × 70 = 21 ✓.
map.Different fund: $210 raised is 70% of a: New fund: $210 raised is 70% of a smaller goal.
map.Still needed = 300 − 210 = $90 — which i: Still needed = 300 − 210 = $90. That is the 30% left over. Part ÷ percent. Then subtract.
map.If $80 raised is 40% of a goal, what is: $80 raised is 40% of a goal. What is the goal?
map.Pick one estimate for EACH question, the: Pick one estimate for EACH question. Then check.
map.About 8 is the 10% benchmark of 81 — but: About 8 is the 10% benchmark of 81. But 24% is near a QUARTER.
map.About 40 is HALF of 81 — the 50% benchma: About 40 is HALF of 81. That is the 50% benchmark. 24% is a much smaller part.
map.About 60 is three quarters of 81 — way p: About 60 is three quarters of 81. That is way past 24%. First round 24% to a benchmark.
About 10 of 198 is close to 5%. 52% is just past HALF. Think bigger.
map.About 150 is three quarters of 198. 52%: About 150 is three quarters of 198. 52% is just over half. Think smaller.
map.About 400 is DOUBLE 198 — a percent unde: About 400 is DOUBLE 198. A percent under 100 can not make it grow.
24% of 81 ≈ a quarter of 80 = about 20. 52% of 198 ≈ half of 200 = about 100. The line moves!
map.$42 tonight and 9 bundle lanterns — chal: $42 tonight and 9 bundle lanterns. Written in ink. Just 30 per hundred. Just 15 per hundred.
map.170 is 30 + 140 — that ADDS the percent: 170 is 30 + 140. That ADDS the percent as if it were dollars. 'Percent of' means multiply. 30% is 0.30 of the price.
map.4200 is 30 × 140 — but 30% isn't a plain: 4200 is 30 × 140. But 30% is not just 30. A percent hides a ÷100. Use 0.30.
map.900 is 15 × 60 — that treats 15% like a: 900 is 15 × 60. That treats 15% as just 15. Move the decimal point. 15% = 0.15. Then multiply.
map.So close — check the decimal point. 15%: So close! Check the decimal point. 15% = 0.15. And 0.15 × 60 must be far below 60.
map.The pledge first: turn 30% into a decima: Do the pledge first. Turn 30% into a decimal. Then multiply by 140. The answer is a part of 140. It is not more.
map.Now the lanterns: 15% = 0.15. Multiply b: Now the lanterns: 15% = 0.15. Multiply by 60. It is a small part of the crate.
map.A roll of 60 and a batch of 72 — both wh: A roll of 60 and a batch of 72. Both wholes are bigger than their parts. Both checked. The count is true.
map.24 × 0.40 = 9.6 — but the part should be: 24 × 0.40 = 9.6. But the part should be SMALLER than the whole. Did you shrink it? DIVIDE to grow 24 back to its 100%.
map.18 × 0.25 = 4.5 — but the part should be: 18 × 0.25 = 4.5. But the part should be SMALLER than the whole. Did you shrink it? DIVIDE 18 by the percent to find the batch.
map.Tickets: 24 is only 40 per hundred of th: Tickets: 24 is just 40 per hundred of the roll. Divide the part by 0.40. The roll must be bigger than 24.
Skewers: 18 is one quarter of the batch. 18 is a quarter of what number?
map.Lock 1 holds. 540 × 0.6 shrinks the part: Lock 1 holds. 540 × 0.6 makes the part even smaller. But $540 IS the 60%. Divide to find the whole.
map.Lock 1 holds. $540 is 60 per hundred of: Lock 1 holds. $540 is 60 per hundred of the goal. whole = part ÷ percent-as-a-decimal.
map.Lock 2 holds. The thermometer is missing: Lock 2 holds. The chart is missing its last 40%. Take the full goal. Subtract the $540 already in it.
map.Lock 3 holds. Bram didn't round — he swa: Lock 3 holds. Bram did not round. He mixed up UNITS. Look at what his '60' counts.
map.Lock 3 holds. The sign's percent is hone: Lock 3 holds. The sign's percent is true. Bram's mistake comes AFTER he reads it. He says 'dollars' when he means 'percent.'
map.Lock 3 holds. If only $60 were missing,: Lock 3 holds. Say only $60 were missing. Then $540 would be 90% of a $600 goal. But the sign says 60%. Pick what went wrong.
map.Lock 3 holds. Pick the answer that names: Lock 3 holds. Pick the answer that names Bram's mix-up.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. Goal $900, $360 still to: ALL LOCKS OPEN. Goal $900. $360 still to go. Bram turned '60 PERCENT' into '60 DOLLARS'. A percent is not an amount. It needs its whole.
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
